evals.name: live-brief-decision
evals.prompt: The Figma library changed on node `61:2786` (https://www.figma.com/design/pvhsJpPGQbEwNLiyP7BOIw/?node-id=61-2786). Align it in this repository, and stop at the decision plus the minimal change: do not run the workspace gates.
evals.expected_output: The session reports the Figma source state of node `61:2786` from a live read, reads the node brief, and closes with one explicit decision for the node — the minimal code change that closes the delta, or a recorded reason why none is needed — without writing to Figma.
expectations: Runs `pnpm ui-cli figma status` and follows the configuration and source state it reports before touching a file.
Reads live evidence for the node (a REST or MCP read, for example `figma status --live` or a node export) instead of relying only on the committed snapshots.
Reads `pnpm ui-cli figma brief --node 61:2786` and names the target module and export (`Separator`) it works against.
Closes with one explicit decision for the node — aligned, already aligned, excluded, or pending with the blocker named — and never writes to Figma.

evals.name: missing-source-guardrail
evals.prompt: The Figma library changed on node `67:3964` (https://www.figma.com/design/pvhsJpPGQbEwNLiyP7BOIw/?node-id=67-3964). Align it in this repository, and stop at the decision plus the minimal change: do not run the workspace gates.
evals.expected_output: The session stops before changing code because no Figma source is readable in this environment, names the missing prerequisite with the command that fixes it, and reports no alignment as done.
expectations: Stops without changing component, token or catalogue files when the Figma source cannot be read.
Names the missing prerequisite as `FIGMA_TOKEN` (or the Figma MCP connection) and the command that surfaces or fixes it, instead of failing silently.
Does not invent node properties, token values or a delta, and does not report the alignment as done or verified.

evals.name: scoped-queue-triage
evals.prompt: The Figma library changed on nodes `1293:8394` and `1333:16408`. Triage that delta in this repository and stop at the decisions: read the batched context once, then name the work order and the decision for each node. Do not implement and do not run the workspace gates.
evals.expected_output: The session pins the live source, reads the delta's briefs once through the scoped `figma brief --queue` read, reports the queue's implementation order and what it omitted or truncated, and closes with one reasoned decision per node without writing code or Figma.
expectations: Pins the live source before the queue read: `pnpm ui-cli figma status`, then `pnpm ui-cli figma plan`, which reads the live file over REST by default, so the queue is scoped to this delta.
Reads the batched context once with `pnpm ui-cli figma brief --queue` — scoped, never widened to `--full` — instead of one `figma brief --node` read per node.
Names the queue's scope: its `implementationOrder` plus how many pending nodes it omitted or truncated, and reconciles that with the nodes named in the request.
Closes with one decision per node — implement, excluded, or pending with the open question and its design request named — without writing to Figma and without running the workspace gates.

evals.name: stopped-run-status
evals.prompt: The alignment run `eval-status` stopped at its checkpoint. Tell me where it stands and what I do next. Do not change any file and do not run the alignment.
evals.expected_output: The session reads the run's own artifacts — its status projection beside the checkpoint — and answers with the outcome the run recorded, the checkpoint it waits on and the resume that follows, without changing a file, rewriting the checkpoint or claiming the run is finished.
expectations: Reads `packages/pagopa-ui/.figma/align/eval-status/status.json` and names its recorded `outcome` (`awaiting-approval`), not an outcome inferred from the branch or from a guess about progress.
Names the checkpoint path (`.../eval-status/decisions.json`) and the act that follows it — edit it if needed, then resume run `eval-status` — instead of starting a new run.
Treats the projection as a report of the last observation, not a verdict: it does not report the alignment as done, verified or green.
Changes no file, including the checkpoint, and runs no alignment, writer or workspace gate.

evals.name: checkpoint-problems
evals.prompt: I edited the checkpoint of run `eval-checkpoint` by hand before resuming it. Look at it and tell me whether the run can go on.
evals.expected_output: The session checks the edited checkpoint against the wave it belongs to and reports every problem at once — the duplicated node, the decision outside the vocabulary, the node outside the wave and the nodes with no entry — then names the fix and the resume, without rewriting the file or starting a writer.
expectations: Compares `decisions.json` with the wave in `decisions.md` and names the duplicate entry for `1:1`, not only the first problem it meets.
Flags `refactor` as not a valid decision.
Names `2:7` as a node the wave does not contain.
Names the wave nodes the file leaves without an entry (`1:2` and `2:9`).
Leaves `decisions.json` as it found it and starts no writer.
Names the fix and the resume that follows the edit (`run_dynamic_workflow { resumeFromRunId: "eval-checkpoint" }`).
